sentences.text: The upper jaw bone of Sinotyrannus features a uniquely curved upper edge that dips inward, contrasting with the outward curve seen in later tyrannosaurs.
Three preserved back vertebrae possess exceptionally tall bony projections along their tops.
The type species is Sinotyrannus kazuoensis.
It inhabited a wet environment characterized by well-watered forests and large lakes.
The environment where Sinotyrannus lived was prone to high levels of volcanism.
Recent research suggests that Sinotyrannus, known from an adult specimen, may be a mature form of the earlier named genus Huaxiagnathus, which is known only from immature specimens.
